agree.reason: Staff who don't want phone work get a low-risk trial through the six-month severance option, seniority-based shift choice and a straight account of the downsides, though the email never mentions the rumours they've already heard and never names a branch habit they'd keep.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'better for everyone' claim and uses only figures the writer was given, but 'I don't have shift lengths or schedules yet' is a claim about what the writer knows that the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only restated: the $1.50 raise is never turned into a yearly amount (about $3,000 for full-time work), and no severance example is given (a ten-year teller would get 20 weeks' pay) that would make each person's choice concrete.

right_comparison.reason: It names the three options plainly (take the role, take severance, or try the role and then leave) and gives the trend behind the closures (44% fewer branch visits and 60% more phone and chat contacts), though it never compares the outcomes of those options side by side for a long-serving teller.

qualification.reason: The commitments have firm dates (February 14 and March 1), but the hedge about missing shift details gives no date for when staff will learn them, even though they need that before deciding.

objections.reason: It meets the main objections directly by admitting the 30% turnover on the phone team, refusing to promise 9-to-5 hours and offering the six-month exit, but it never addresses the rumours or why staff learned about the closures that way.

fit.reason: It is an email from the COO of roughly 420 words with a clear subject line and scannable sections, which matches the requested form.
